setup.tagline: First-time setup — we guide you one step at a time.
setup.welcome.title: Welcome to RNode and the Bitcoin Ecosystem.
setup.welcome.body: This box is your home internet router and a Bitcoin full node. Setup takes a few minutes — just follow each screen. Join Wi‑Fi rnode with the password printed on the label, or use a LAN cable.
setup.security.title: Security
setup.security.body: We are now going to make sure that your connection to your router is secure, which means it is safe. To start the process, click on the Enable Secure Connection button below. This will download a small file to this computer. Open the file and follow the prompts; this will enable the secure connection; you will need to provide the password to this device.
setup.choice.title: Setup
setup.choice.body: Choose how you want to set up this router.
setup.choice.quick_note: Recommended for non-technical people — the factory settings are used, which is fine.
setup.choice.guided_note: Recommended for technical people — customise the Wi‑Fi name, LAN IP range and node choice.
setup.quick.title: Quick Start
setup.quick.body: Set a new router password and a new Wi‑Fi password (not the factory password printed on the label). Everything else uses the factory defaults (Wi‑Fi name rnode, Bitcoin Core node, automatic internet).
setup.pppoe.title: Internet provider login
setup.pppoe.body: No internet address yet. If your ISP gave you a username and password, enter them here — or skip and set up internet later in Settings.
setup.password.title: Router password
setup.password.body: Create a new router password. You will need it later for Settings and Router settings. Do not reuse the temporary factory password.
setup.wan.title: Internet
setup.wan.pppoe: My ISP needs a username and password
setup.wifi.title: Wi‑Fi
setup.wifi.body: Choose a new Wi‑Fi name and password that phones and laptops will use. You cannot keep the factory password.
setup.wifi.body_onwifi: You are on Wi‑Fi. Saving does not disconnect you: the new name and password take effect when you finish Setup — then join the new network with the new password.
setup.wifi.none: Wi‑Fi is not available on this unit.
setup.wifi.ssid_hint: Default is rnode. You can change it.
setup.wifi.key_hint: At least 8 characters (WPA2: 8–63). Must not be the factory password printed on the label.
setup.node.title: Bitcoin node
setup.lan.title: Advanced — LAN address
setup.lan.body: Most homes should leave this alone and tap Continue. Only change LAN IP if someone told you to.
setup.done.title: You’re set
setup.done.body: Setup is finished. Next you will see Node Status while the Bitcoin node starts and catches up with the network (this can take a long time — that is normal).
setup.restart.title: Restarting Router to Apply Selected Settings
setup.welcome.body_nowifi: This box is your home internet router and a Bitcoin full node. Setup takes a few minutes — just follow each screen. Wi‑Fi is off until Setup is finished — connect a LAN cable from this box to your computer.
setup.welcome.join: Join Wi‑Fi rnode with the password printed on the label — or plug a LAN cable from this box into your computer.
setup.welcome.join_nowifi: Plug a LAN cable from this box into your computer (Wi‑Fi is off until Setup is finished).
setup.locale.tz_nearest: Your browser's timezone ({zone}) is not in the list, so {chosen} (the same time now) is selected. Please check it below — it also sets the Wi‑Fi country.

api.node.bad_impl: Bitcoin Core is the only node software on this router.

api.node.knots_dropped: Bitcoin Core is the only node software on this router.

nodesw.auth.note: Every change on this page needs the router root username and password (the same as for Router settings).
nodesw.auth.required: Enter the router username and password.
nodesw.confirm.restart: If this node software is in use, the node will restart.
nodesw.err.non_json: The node service sent an unexpected reply (HTTP {status}). Try again in a moment.
nodesw.err.status_failed: Could not read the node software status.
nodesw.footer: The blockchain data stays on the M.2 drive — installing or rolling back never reformats it.
nodesw.install.accepted: Upload received — installing. This can take a few minutes.
nodesw.install.bad_name: The file name should contain aarch64 (the official Linux build for this router).
nodesw.install.body: Upload an official Bitcoin Core *-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz file from bitcoincore.org. It is stored on the M.2 drive under node-bin/. The previous version is kept so you can roll back. The blockchain data is never deleted.
nodesw.install.confirm_keep: The previous version (if any) is kept so you can roll back.
nodesw.install.installing: Installing {name} — this can take a few minutes…
nodesw.install.no_file: Choose the official release file (aarch64 .tar.gz) first.
nodesw.install.title: Install or replace Bitcoin Core
nodesw.install.wallet_ack: Tick the wallet backup box before installing.
nodesw.knots_dropped: This router runs Bitcoin Core. Bitcoin Knots is no longer part of btcrouternode (since build 120): a router that ran Knots switched to Core by itself, keeping its chain data.
nodesw.op.install.ok: Bitcoin Core installed. The blockchain data was kept.
nodesw.op.rollback.ok: Rolled back Bitcoin Core. The blockchain data was kept.
nodesw.op.slow: This is taking longer than expected — check Node Status.
nodesw.rollback.body: Restores the previously installed Bitcoin Core (if there is one).
nodesw.rollback.confirm_title: Roll back {name} to the previous version?
nodesw.rollback.title: Roll back to the previous version
nodesw.rollback.wallet_ack: Tick the wallet backup box before rolling back.
nodesw.tagline: Bitcoin Core on this router: install an official release (aarch64) or go back to the previous one. The blockchain stays on the same drive.
nodesw.wallet.ack: I understand the risk and have (or accept needing) an offline wallet backup before changing the node software.
nodesw.wallet.dir_present: A wallet folder is present in the node's shared data directory.
nodesw.wallet.warn: Wallet detected on this appliance. Replacing the node software is not recommended when a wallet is present. The keys are meant to stay on the shared drive, but if the wallet fails to load after a change you may need your offline backup (or descriptor recovery material) to regain access to your funds.
status.disk.action.at_risk: Replace the M.2 drive soon and contact support. The node keeps running for now.
status.disk.action.attention: Plan to replace the M.2 drive. The node keeps running.
status.disk.action.failed: The node cannot use this drive. Contact support.
status.disk.power_lost.body: The router lost power without shutting down in the last 7 days. A small UPS helps protect the blockchain drive.
status.disk.power_lost.title: Power was lost
status.disk.reason.backup_failed: The drive's internal power-loss backup has failed.
status.disk.reason.controller_not_live: The M.2 drive is not responding.
status.disk.reason.drive_missing: The M.2 drive is not detected.
status.disk.reason.filesystem_errors: The drive's file system has reported errors.
status.disk.reason.media_errors: The drive has reported data errors.
status.disk.reason.media_read_only: The drive has become read-only and can no longer store new blocks.
status.disk.reason.not_mounted: The blockchain drive is not mounted.
status.disk.reason.read_only: The blockchain drive has switched to read-only.
status.disk.reason.reliability_degraded: The drive reports that its reliability is degraded.
status.disk.reason.smart_unavailable: Drive health data could not be read.
status.disk.reason.spare_dropping: The drive's spare capacity is dropping.
status.disk.reason.spare_low: The drive is running out of spare capacity.
status.disk.reason.temperature_critical: The drive is too hot — check that the router has airflow.
status.disk.reason.temperature_critical_: The drive is too hot ({temp} °C) — check that the router has airflow.
status.disk.reason.wear_high: The drive is past 80 % of its rated write life.
status.disk.reason.wear_out: The drive has used its rated write life.
status.error.container_start_failed: The node service could not start.
status.error.node_failed_to_become_ready: The node started but did not become ready.
status.error.rpc_error: The node reported an error when asked for its status.
status.error.service_state: The node service is not running ({state}).
status.error.storage_not_mounted: The blockchain drive (M.2) is not mounted.
status.error.storage_not_ready: The blockchain drive (M.2) is not ready.
status.footer: This page is for the Bitcoin node. For Wi‑Fi and the firewall, use Router settings (LuCI) in the menu.
status.low_space: The blockchain drive is running low on free space. This node keeps the full blockchain (it is not pruned) — free up space soon.
status.op.boot_recover: Node is initialising — recovering after a restart.
status.op.conf: Applying node settings — restarting the node.
status.op.initializing_start: Node is initialising — starting Bitcoin. The status will update when it is ready.
status.op.initializing_storage: Node is initialising — waiting for the M.2 drive.
status.op.initializing_verify: Node is initialising — loading and checking the chain database. This can take a few minutes after a power loss.
status.op.reboot: Stopping the node and restarting the router.
status.op.reindex: Repairing the chain database. This uses the blocks already on the M.2 drive — it is not downloading the blockchain again. Keep the power on; this can take many hours.
status.op.reindex_full: Rebuilding the block index and chain database — not downloading the blockchain again.
status.op.set: Setup is applying the node choice.
status.op.shutdown: Stopping the node and shutting down the router.
status.op.update: Node update in progress. The status will refresh when it is ready.
status.op.upgrade: Router software update in progress (the blockchain is not touched).
status.op.waiting_clock: Waiting for the correct time. The router sets its clock from the internet; the node starts by itself as soon as it has the time (your blockchain is fine).
status.recovery.chainstate: The node cannot start until the chain database is repaired. This rebuilds it from the blocks already on the M.2 drive — it does not download the blockchain again.
status.reindex.accepted: Repair starting. The status will show its progress. The blocks on the M.2 drive are kept — this is not a fresh download.
status.reindex.body: The node cannot start until the local chain database is repaired. This re-checks the blocks already on the M.2 drive and rebuilds the chain state — it does not download the blockchain again. It can take many hours; keep the power on.
status.reindex.keep_power: Keep the power on. This page refreshes automatically.
status.reindex.need_auth: Enter the router username and password to start the repair.
status.reindex.start_failed: The repair could not be started — see the node log.
status.reindex.title: Chain database needs repair
status.reindex.type_word: Type {word} to confirm the chain database repair.
status.sub.busy: Please wait — the node software is being changed or updated. This page will refresh automatically when the node is ready.
status.sub.coming_up: Please wait — the node is starting up. This page refreshes automatically.
status.sub.down: Check the blockchain drive (M.2) and the node service.
status.sub.initialising: Please wait — the node is starting up. This page refreshes automatically; no action needed.
status.sub.reindex: Checking the blocks already on the M.2 drive — not downloading the blockchain again. Keep the power on; this can take many hours. This page refreshes automatically.
status.sub.synced: Checking new blocks as they arrive.
status.sub.waiting: The router is up. Status data is still starting.
status.sub.waiting_clock: Make sure the router's internet (WAN) cable is plugged in. Nothing needs repairing; this page refreshes automatically.
status.tagline: Full node status for this router. Sync, peers, and storage at a glance.

api.settings.bad_size: The image size is out of range (8–256 MiB).
api.settings.blocked_key: bitcoin.conf was not saved: {key} cannot be changed here — this product depends on it.
api.settings.conf_not_started: bitcoin.conf saved, but the node did not start again. Check your last change, or see the node log.
api.settings.conf_restarted: bitcoin.conf saved; the node has restarted.
api.settings.conf_saved_restarting: bitcoin.conf saved; the node is restarting.

api.settings.lang_updated: Language updated for these pages and Router settings.
api.settings.method: The request was not valid (POST required). Reload the page and try again.
api.settings.missing_product_keys: bitcoin.conf was not saved: settings this product needs (datadir, bind, rpcbind, prune, disablewallet) are missing or changed.
api.settings.no_changes: There were no settings to save.
api.settings.no_conf: bitcoin.conf was not found on the router.
api.settings.no_sysupgrade: The upgrade tool (sysupgrade) is not available on this router.
api.settings.node_busy: Another node operation is still running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
api.settings.node_starting_full: The Bitcoin node is starting with a full reindex. Keep the power on — this can take many hours. The blockchain is not downloaded again.
api.settings.node_starting_reindex: The Bitcoin node is starting with a reindex. Keep the power on — checking can take many hours. The blockchain is not downloaded again.
api.settings.op_interrupted: The node operation stopped unexpectedly — check Node Status and try again.
api.settings.origin_denied: A request from another website was refused.

api.settings.reindex_full_running: Full reindex running — keep the power on.
api.settings.reindex_in_progress: A reindex is already running. Keep the power on and wait for it to finish.
api.settings.reindex_not_started: The node did not start the reindex — see the node log.
api.settings.reindex_running: Reindex running — keep the power on.
api.settings.sha256_mismatch: The SHA256 does not match. Download the image again and paste the checksum from the release page. (No upgrade was started.)
api.settings.sha256_required: Paste the SHA256 checksum from the release page before upgrading.
api.settings.shutting_down: Stopping the Bitcoin node and shutting down…
api.settings.start_failed: The Bitcoin node did not start — see the node log.
api.settings.stop_failed: The Bitcoin node is still running after the stop request. Try again.
api.settings.temp: The router could not create a temporary file. Try again.
api.settings.tls_failed: Could not create a new certificate: {detail}

api.settings.unsigned_image: This image is not signed. Only signed RNode releases can be installed. (No upgrade was started.)
api.settings.upgrade_keep: Checksum verified — the upgrade is starting (keeping router settings). The device will reboot. The blockchain on the M.2 drive is not wiped.
api.settings.upgrade_reset: Checksum verified — the upgrade is starting (resetting router settings). The device will reboot. The blockchain on the M.2 drive is not wiped.
api.settings.wan_denied: Changes can only be made from your home network (LAN).
settings.addpc.after: — type it with http://. It shows Enable Secure Connection and the steps for that computer, then carries on to your router securely. After a factory reset or a renewed certificate, every computer does this once again.
settings.addpc.before: On the new computer (Windows, Mac or Linux), open a browser and go to

settings.adv.confirm_body:
Advanced editing — the keys this product depends on cannot change.
The Bitcoin node will restart. The chain data is kept.
settings.adv.confirm_title: Save raw bitcoin.conf and restart the node?
settings.adv.err_type: Type {word} to save with the raw editor.
settings.adv.intro: Edit bitcoin.conf directly. Changes to keys this product depends on (datadir, bind, prune, disablewallet, …) are refused. Saving needs ADVANCED and SAVE typed below, and the router password.
settings.adv.saving: Saving bitcoin.conf and restarting the node…
settings.adv.title: Bitcoin Node Configuration - Experienced User
settings.auth_note: Every change on this page needs the router root username and password (the same login as Router settings).
settings.conf.confirm_body:
Only the settings on this form are changed.
The Bitcoin node will restart. The chain data is kept.
settings.conf.confirm_title: Save bitcoin.conf and restart the node?
settings.conf.intro: Only these safe settings can be changed here. Saving restarts the node. The settings this product depends on (datadir, RPC bind, prune, wallet) stay fixed.
settings.conf.title: Bitcoin Node Configuration - Beginner User
settings.confirm.type_restart: Type {word} to confirm (this restarts the Bitcoin node)
settings.err.auth_required: Enter the router username and password.
settings.err.non_json: The router sent an unexpected answer (HTTP {status}). {text}
settings.landrop.body:
Your computer may show Ethernet as disconnected while the router restarts.
Leave the cable plugged in. Turn the wired connection back on if {os} turns it off.
Keep the progress tab open. Do not unplug or switch off the router.
settings.landrop.title: {os} will turn Ethernet off
settings.lang.confirm_body:
These pages and Router settings will both use: {lang}
This needs the router root password.
settings.lang.intro: Changes the language of these pages and of Router settings together. The timezone stays as chosen in first-time Setup.
settings.lang.label: Language
settings.lang.title: Language
settings.node.intro: Controls the Bitcoin node only. The router itself keeps running — it is not restarted or shut down. The chain data on the M.2 drive is kept.
settings.node.reindex.label: ReIndex Node
settings.node.reindex.progress: Reindex in progress. Keep the power on — this uses blocks already on the M.2 drive and does not download the blockchain again.
settings.node.start.confirm_body: The Bitcoin node (bitcoind) will start with the chain data already on the M.2 drive.
settings.node.start.confirm_body_full:
The Bitcoin node (bitcoind) will start with the chain data already on the M.2 drive.
You chose: Also rebuild the block index.
This rebuilds the block index and the chain database from every block file already on the M.2 drive. It does not download the blockchain again.
This is slower than Repair chain database. Keep the power on; it can take many hours.
settings.node.start.confirm_body_reindex:
The Bitcoin node (bitcoind) will start with the chain data already on the M.2 drive.
You chose: Repair chain database (usual).
This checks the chain database against the blocks already on the M.2 drive. It does not download the blockchain again.
Keep the power on; this can take many hours.
settings.node.start.confirm_title_full: Start the Bitcoin node with a full reindex?
settings.node.start.confirm_title_reinde: Start the Bitcoin node with reindex?
settings.node.start.desc: Starts the Bitcoin node (bitcoind) with the chain data already on the M.2 drive. Available only when the node is stopped — stop it first, then start it. The optional ReIndex Node repairs the local chain database from blocks already on the M.2 drive — it does not download the blockchain again.
settings.node.start.err_running: Stop the Bitcoin node first. Start is only available when the node is stopped.
settings.node.start.title: Start node
settings.node.stop.confirm_body:
The Bitcoin node (bitcoind) will stop. The chain data on the M.2 drive is kept.
Use Start node when you want it running again.
settings.node.stop.desc: Stops the Bitcoin node (bitcoind). The router stays on.
settings.node.stop.title: Stop node
settings.node.title: Node start / stop
settings.power.going_down: The router is restarting or shutting down…
settings.power.intro: Controls the whole appliance (the router) — not the same as starting or stopping the node above. Reboot and shutdown always stop the Bitcoin node first, so its chain data is saved cleanly. The same happens if you reboot from Router settings.
settings.power.title: Appliance power
settings.reboot.confirm_body:
The Bitcoin node will be stopped first.
The router will restart. The network drops for a short while.
settings.reboot.desc: Restarts the router. The network drops for a short while.
settings.reboot.title: Reboot appliance
settings.reset.after: You will be taken to a full reset page that shows the progress, then to first-time Setup.
settings.reset.confirm_body:
Router settings return to the factory defaults.
The admin password becomes the factory password again.
You will go through first-time Setup again.
The blockchain on the M.2 drive is NOT wiped.
settings.reset.intro: Restores router settings to the factory defaults (network, firewall, admin password) and starts first-time Setup again. The blockchain on the M.2 drive is not wiped. The Bitcoin node is stopped cleanly first.
settings.reset.title: Factory reset
settings.shutdown.confirm_body:
The Bitcoin node will be stopped first.
The router will turn off. You must turn it on again yourself.
settings.shutdown.desc: Turns the appliance off. You must turn it on again yourself.
settings.shutdown.title: Shutdown appliance
settings.tagline: Upgrade the router software, adjust bitcoin.conf, start or stop the Bitcoin node, and restart or shut down the router. The blockchain is never wiped.
settings.tls.confirm_body:
A new certificate is created for this router.
Every device must install it again before the secure pages work there.
settings.tls.desc: Creates a new certificate for this router's secure pages. Every computer that installed the old one must add the router again (see Add another computer above). Use this if a device that trusted this router was lost or sold.
settings.tls.fingerprint: Current certificate SHA-256 fingerprint (compare it with what the installer shows on a new device):
settings.tls.title: Renew HTTPS certificate
settings.tls.unrestricted: Not restricted (older certificate) — renew it so new devices can install it.
settings.upgrade.err.filename: Expected a file name ending in sysupgrade.itb (or .bin).
settings.upgrade.err.mismatch: SHA256 mismatch — the file does not match the checksum. Download the image again and paste the hash from the release page.
settings.upgrade.err.network: Upload failed — network error. Check the network connection and try again.
settings.upgrade.err.no_sha: Paste the SHA256 checksum from the release page (64 hex characters).
settings.upgrade.err.sdcard: SD card images (*.img.gz) cannot be used here. Choose a *sysupgrade.itb file.
settings.upgrade.err.timeout: The upload timed out. Try again on a stable network connection.
settings.upgrade.hint.keep: Keeps Wi‑Fi, the admin password and network settings. First-time Setup will not run again.
settings.upgrade.hint.reset: Wi‑Fi, the admin password and network settings return to factory defaults. First-time Setup runs again. The blockchain on the M.2 drive is still not wiped.
settings.upgrade.intro: Upload a BPI-R4 sysupgrade image (*sysupgrade.itb — not the SD card image *.img.gz). Paste the SHA256 checksum from the release page (required — it checks the file before installing). Choose whether to keep your router settings (default) or reset them to factory defaults. The blockchain on the M.2 drive is never wiped. Bitcoin Core updates are on Node software.
settings.upgrade.link_dropped: Connection dropped after the upload — waiting for the reboot
settings.upgrade.p.mismatch_detail: The file does not match the SHA256 you pasted
settings.upgrade.p.verifying: Checking the SHA256 on the router, then installing
settings.upgrade.reset_aria: Reset router settings to factory defaults
settings.upgrade.response_cut: Router rebooting (answer cut off) — waiting to reconnect
settings.upgrade.sha_hint: Copy the hash from the same place you downloaded the image (for example the .sha256 file or the website). You can paste a full sha256sum line — only the hash is used.
settings.upgrade.sha_hint_short: Copy the hash from the release page (or the .sha256 file). It is required before upgrading.
settings.upgrade.sha_placeholder: Paste the 64-character hash from the release page
settings.upgrade.started: Firmware upgrade started — opening the progress page…
settings.upgrade.timeout_wait: No answer from the router after the upload — waiting for the reboot
settings.upgrade.title: Appliance upgrade
settings.upgrade.uploaded: Upload finished — the router is checking the checksum…
settings.upgrade.uploading_http: Uploading — the router checks the SHA256 before installing (normal on HTTP).
settings.upgrade.uploading_ok: Local checksum OK — uploading… keep this page open.
luci.entry.mistake: If you opened this by mistake, return to the node status page (no router password needed there).
luci.entry.note: Log in as root with the router password you chose in Setup. Router settings cannot be opened from the internet.
luci.entry.secure: Admin login is required. This page is not LuCI — it only routes you to login or back to the Bitcoin node dashboard.
luci.entry.title: Router settings (LuCI)
luci.return.title: Log out of router settings and open Node Status
reset.copy: Keep this page open. Each reset step has its own bar that counts down even if this computer briefly loses the router. The Bitcoin node is stopped, router settings are restored, then the appliance reboots. The blockchain on the M.2 is not wiped. Your computer may show Ethernet or Wi-Fi as disconnected while the router restarts — that is normal. Leave the cable plugged in; if Ubuntu turns LAN off, click it back on. Do not power-cycle the router.
reset.hint: When this finishes, first-run Setup opens automatically.
reset.idle: No factory reset in progress. Use Settings → Reset to factory defaults.
reset.idle_hint: This page stays open so it does not send you to a Settings or secure page that is not ready yet.
reset.looking: Looking for {url} — opening Setup when it is ready…
reset.page_title: Factory Reset in Progress — Bitcoin Node
reset.rebooting: Factory reset is restarting the router.
reset.title: Factory Reset in Progress
reset.waiting_back: Waiting for {url} to come back. Opening Setup.
reset.warn: Do NOT Power Cycle the router — reset in progress

setup.err.pw_short: Password must be at least 8 characters.

setup.finish.lan_moved: Your computer will get a new address. If you are on Wi‑Fi, turn it off and on. If you use a cable, unplug it and plug it back in.

setup.finish.title: Applying your settings
setup.lan.note: These values are saved and applied when you finish Setup. The home network does not change until then.
setup.lan.saved: LAN saved. It applies when you finish Setup.
setup.node.core_only: This router runs Bitcoin Core, a full Bitcoin node that checks every block and transaction for itself. It keeps the whole blockchain on the router's own drive.
setup.password.step1: Type a new password in the first box (at least 8 characters).
setup.password.step2: Type the same password again in the second box.
setup.phone.after: After Setup, phones and tablets can use the new Wi‑Fi as normal.
setup.phone.body: Setup starts by making the connection to your router secure, and phones and tablets can’t do that easily. Please do Setup from a laptop or computer:
setup.phone.join: On the computer, join Wi‑Fi rnode with the password on the router’s sticker — or plug a cable into one of the router’s LAN ports.
setup.phone.open: Setup opens by itself. If it does not, open a browser and go to http://192.168.1.254
setup.phone.title: Please use a laptop or computer
setup.quick.wan_down: No internet address yet — you can still finish setup and configure internet later.
setup.restart.copy: Please wait — do not unplug the box. When it is ready, this page should open Node Status by itself. If nothing happens after a minute, type the address below into the browser address bar and press Enter.
setup.security.download_tip: Important — browser downloads: After you click the ‘Enable Secure Connection’ button, watch the top right of the browser (or the downloads arrow). The browser will ask to Allow, Save, or Keep the file being downloaded (this is common in Firefox). You must click that option, otherwise the file will not download. The file should save to your Downloads folder, not open as a page of text. You should be able to open the file from your browser.
setup.tls.help.linux_other: Another Linux? Use the Terminal command box above (Ctrl + Alt + T, paste with Ctrl + Shift + V, Enter, your password).
setup.tls.help.mac_finished: The secure Setup page opens by itself. If it does not, click I’ve finished — continue.
setup.tls.help.mac_password: When your Mac asks for your password, type it and click Update Settings.
setup.tls.linux_alt: Another Linux, or App Center did not open? Use the Terminal instead: press Ctrl + Alt + T, paste this command with Ctrl + Shift + V, press Enter and type your password (nothing shows as you type — that is normal). Firefox closes for a moment and reopens on the secure Setup page by itself.
setup.tls.mac.allow: Your browser asks to open Script Editor — click Allow.
setup.tls.mac.click_above: Click the orange Enable Secure Connection button above.
setup.tls.mac.click_below: Click the orange Enable Secure Connection button below.
setup.tls.mac.close: The secure Setup page opens by itself. Close Script Editor and click Delete (or Don’t Save) — the script is not needed again.
setup.tls.mac.password: Your Mac asks for your password — type it and click Update Settings.
setup.tls.mac.run: Script Editor opens with a short script. Click the ▶ Run button (top left of the Script Editor window).
setup.tls.mac_alt: Script Editor did not open? Copy this command into Terminal instead (⌘ Command + Space, type Terminal, press Return, paste with ⌘ Command + V, press Return, then type your password when asked):
setup.tls.ok_luci_warn: Secure connection OK. If Router settings still warns later, fully quit the browser once.
setup.tls.pending: Secure check still pending. Fully quit the browser (all windows), reopen this Setup page, then tap I’ve finished again — or Skip for now and finish this later.
setup.tls.ready: Secure connection ready — opening the secure page…
setup.tls.reopening: Reopening this page securely so the new certificate applies…
setup.tls.skip_note: Prefer to skip? Tap Skip for now. You can finish later from
setup.tls.skip_note_end: . Until the certificate is installed, the browser may keep showing a warning on Node Status and Router settings (same certificate).
setup.tls.stalled: The browser does not trust the router yet. Finish the installer (it asks for your computer password in the Terminal or a system dialog), then restart the browser if it was open during the install. Or use Skip for now to continue without a secure connection.
setup.tls.unreachable: Secure connection is not reachable right now. Wait a moment and tap I’ve finished again — or Skip for now and finish this later.
setup.tls.watch_start: Open the downloaded file (or run the Terminal command) — nothing installs by itself. Watching for the secure connection…
setup.tls.watch_waiting: Still waiting for the installer — it asks for your computer password itself, never on this page.
setup.wait.still: Still waiting — reconnect to the router's network, then use the link below.
setup.wait.stuck: If this page does not move on,
setup.wait.title: Please wait
setup.wan.help: When it says connected, tap the orange Continue. If it fails: try Try again, or My ISP needs a username and password, or Skip for now and finish internet later.
setup.wan.intro: We are checking whether this box can reach the internet through your modem (automatic setup — you usually do nothing).
setup.wan.no_address: No address yet — check the WAN cable, or your ISP may need a login.
setup.wan.pppoe_note: Your internet provider gave you a username and password. Type them exactly as on the paper / email from your ISP.
setup.welcome.ready: When you are ready, tap Continue below.
setup.welcome.wan: Leave the other cable plugged into your modem / wall internet (WAN) if you have one.
setup.wifi.saved: Wi‑Fi saved. It applies when you finish Setup.
setup.wifi.saved_next: Wi‑Fi saved. It applies when you finish Setup. Set a router password next.
setup.wifi.saving_body: Saving your new network name and password. They apply when Setup finishes. Next you will set the router password.
setup.wifi.step_country: Country code is usually already set from your timezone — change only if wrong (e.g. AU, US, GB).
setup.wifi.step_name: Network name is already filled as rnode — change it only if you want a different name.
setup.wifi.step_password: Type a Wi‑Fi password (at least 8 characters), then type it again to confirm.
setup.wifi.step_save: Tap Save Wi‑Fi. Settings apply when you finish Setup — this computer stays on the factory network until then.
shell.build.title: Product version of this router — quote it when you report a problem.
shell.build.unknown_title: The product version was not found on this router.
tls.add.body: This computer does not have a secure connection to your router yet. It takes about a minute: click Enable Secure Connection and follow the steps below. This page carries on to your router by itself when it is done.
tls.add.checking: Checking whether this computer already has a secure connection…
tls.add.title: Add this computer
tls.footer: Public certificates are not available for a home LAN IP. This local trust step is the supported path. Reinstalling the router from scratch creates a new certificate — repeat this step once if the browser warns again.
tls.hint.linux: Open the downloaded file — App Center opens: Install, then your password. The secure page reopens by itself.
tls.hint.mac: Click Allow, then the ▶ Run button in Script Editor, then type your Mac password.
tls.hint.windows: If the browser asks Allow / Save / Keep (Firefox often does), click that first. Then open the file from Downloads and approve the Windows prompts.
tls.landrop.auto: Turn on Connect automatically for that wired connection so it comes back after a restart.
tls.landrop.keep_open: Keep the progress tab open. Do not power-cycle the router.
tls.landrop.shows: {os} will show Ethernet as disconnected when the router restarts. That is {os} NetworkManager, not a failed update.
tls.landrop.turn_on: If {os} turns LAN off, open Settings → Network and click the wired connection back on.
tls.linux.open_deb: Click the downloaded file rnode-secure-connection.deb (Firefox: the downloads arrow, top right). App Center opens — click Install.
tls.linux.reopen: Your browser reopens on the secure Setup page by itself (Firefox closes for a moment first). If it does not, close the browser and open it again.
tls.mac.allow: When the browser asks to open Script Editor, click Allow.
tls.mac.password: When your Mac asks for your password, type it and click Update Settings. The secure page opens by itself. Close Script Editor without saving.
tls.mac.run: In Script Editor click ▶ Run (top left).
tls.outcome.after: After you trust this router on your device,
tls.phone.body: The secure connection to this router is set up from a laptop or computer (Windows, Mac or Linux). Phones and tablets can’t do that easily.
tls.phone.title: Please use a laptop or computer
tls.step.click_cta: Click the orange Enable Secure Connection button.
tls.tagline: One-time HTTPS trust — then no browser warnings.
tls.tip.download: Important — downloads: After you tap the orange button, look near the top of the browser (or the downloads arrow). If the browser asks to Allow, Save, or Keep the file (this is common in Firefox), you must click that — otherwise the file never finishes downloading.
tls.tip.firefox: Firefox download step: After you tap the orange button, look at the top of the Firefox window or the downloads arrow. You must click Allow or Save File — otherwise the file never downloads. Choose Save File, not “Open with”.
tls.win.allow: Windows asks “Do you want to allow this app to make changes?” — click Yes.
tls.win.done: The secure Setup page opens by itself and the black window closes on its own.
tls.win.keep: If your browser asks about the download, click Keep (Edge: click ⋯ next to the file, then Keep).
tls.win.open_file: Click the file install-bitcoin-node-trust.bat in the browser’s downloads list.
tls.win.run: Windows asks whether to run it — click Run. (A blue box “Windows protected your PC”? Click More info, then Run anyway.)
upgrade.copy: Keep this page open. In-place update has four steps — each bar fills and marks Done before the next starts. Firmware write can take several minutes. The blockchain on the M.2 is not wiped. Your computer may show Ethernet or Wi-Fi as disconnected while the router restarts — that is normal. Leave the cable plugged in; if Ubuntu turns LAN off, click it back on. Do not power-cycle the router.
upgrade.copy_keep: Keep this page open. The Bitcoin node is stopped cleanly, then the new firmware is installed and the router restarts. Router settings are kept. The blockchain on the M.2 is not wiped.
upgrade.copy_reset: Keep this page open. The Bitcoin node is stopped cleanly, then the new firmware is installed and the router restarts. Router settings are reset to factory defaults (Setup will run again). The blockchain on the M.2 is not wiped.
upgrade.failed_detail: The firmware update failed on the router.
upgrade.failed_warn: No update was applied — the router is still running the previous firmware.
upgrade.hint_keep: When this finishes, Node Status opens automatically.
upgrade.hint_reset: When this finishes, first-run Setup opens automatically.
upgrade.idle: No firmware update in progress. Use Settings → Appliance upgrade.
upgrade.looking: Looking for {url} — opening the working page when it is ready…
upgrade.page_title: Firmware Update in Progress — Bitcoin Node
upgrade.reboot_detail: Router restarting — do NOT power-cycle. Waiting for the router to come back…
upgrade.stalled: The update stalled — trying again on the router…
upgrade.title: Firmware Update in Progress
upgrade.waiting_back: Waiting for {url} to come back. Confirming the page is ready.
upgrade.warn: Do NOT Power Cycle the router — update in progress
wait.detail.active: {step} — about {s}s on this step. Do not power-cycle.
wait.handoff.https_untrusted: The router is back, but Node Status needs a trusted HTTPS connection. Stay on this page — do not power-cycle.
wait.handoff.status: Waiting for Node Status to come ready at {url} …
wait.lan_back: Waiting for the router LAN to come back…
wait.lan_drop: Your computer may show Ethernet or Wi-Fi as disconnected while the router restarts. That is normal. Leave the cable plugged in. If Ubuntu turns LAN off, click it back on. Do not power-cycle the router.
wait.reboot_detail: Finishing the restart — do NOT power-cycle…
wait.remaining: About {remain}s remaining · {elapsed}s elapsed — Do NOT Power Cycle
